what: Decode of twitter.cbor (402814 bytes) into test_binding, MiB/s, with the heap of glibc kept: arm old reads tags 28 and 29 always (main 2829e7d); arm off has the template parameter sharedrefs off by default; arm on is the same header with sharedrefs::on.
why: The run of 2026-10-04 before this one had a noise of 10 percent between two builds of one arm. The owner asked to reduce it.
how: As before, with GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.trim_threshold=1073741824:glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=1073741824:glibc.malloc.top_pad=268435456, so glibc keeps the pages of the tree between iterations. setarch -R is refused in the container. 3 rounds, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving.
finding: The two builds of each arm now differ by at most 3 MiB/s (1.2 percent). off reads 235/236 against 241/244 for old and 241/241 for on: switching the code for tags 28 and 29 off does not make decode faster; it reads about 2 percent slower.
